mainTopic: Whether בית דין takes back interest, and what אביי and רבא really argue about. Then, the prohibitions on blemished animals for the מזבח and why 'לה׳' is needed to include the שעיר המשתלח.
overview: The amud opens with a ruling: אבק רבית is not taken back by בית דין, and רבי יוחנן says even רבית קצוצה is not. The גמרא had tried to link this to the argument of אביי and רבא about whether a forbidden act still takes effect. It rejects that link, because the interest argument comes from פסוקים. Three sources are brought for רבי יוחנן, and one source, 'וחי אחיך עמך', is brought for רבי אלעזר. So what do אביי and רבא argue about? One version says they argue only about the general starting rule. Another version says they argue about returning רבית קצוצה, but אביי's own case of the cloak shows he also takes it back, so the גמרא returns to the first answer. Then a new topic begins: a ברייתא lists the prohibitions on bringing a blemished animal to the מזבח, and it uses 'לה׳' to include the שעיר המשתלח. רבא explains why another ברייתא uses the same word to exclude it. The גמרא then asks why 'לה׳' is needed at all, since the lottery only works on fit animals. רב יוסף and רבא each answer with a case where a goat becomes the שעיר המשתלח without a lottery.

steps.title: Is interest taken back by judges?
steps.stepSummary: אבק רבית is not taken back by בית דין. רבי יוחנן says that even רבית קצוצה is not taken back.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Dust of interest' is not taken back by the judges. And רבי יוחנן says: even fixed, explicit interest is not taken back by the judges.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote about whether בית דין forces a lender to give back interest he already collected. רבי יוחנן goes furthest: no kind of interest is taken back by the judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels of interest. רבית קצוצה is fixed interest agreed on up front, which the Torah forbids. אבק רבית is only a 'hint' of interest, forbidden by the רבנן. Everyone agrees the judges don't take back אבק רבית. רבי יוחנן goes further and says that even רבית קצוצה stays with the lender as far as בית דין is concerned.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Dust of interest': a mild, indirect form of interest, forbidden by the רבנן
Fixed interest agreed on up front; forbidden by the Torah
Taken back (forced out of the lender's hands) by the judges

steps.confusionAlert: Saying the interest is 'not taken back by judges' does NOT mean taking interest is allowed. It is still a serious sin. The only question is whether בית דין forces the money to be returned.

phrases.english: 'Dust of interest' is not taken back by the judges,
and רבי יוחנן says:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ רִבִּית קְצוּצָה אֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה בְּדַיָּינִין.
phrases.english: even fixed interest is not taken back by the judges.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ רִבִּית קְצוּצָה אֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה בְּדַיָּינִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the earlier quoted argument about returning interest, which the גמרא was trying to connect to אביי and רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, no interest (not even רבית קצוצה) is taken back by the judges.

steps.title: Their argument is about verses, not logic
steps.stepSummary: One sage rejects the link: רבי יוחנן and the other view do not argue over logic. They argue over how to read פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do they argue there about logic? They argue there about verses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea that this interest argument proves anything about the general question of whether a forbidden act 'works'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attempted link said: if a forbidden act takes effect, the interest belongs to the lender and stays with him. That would explain רבי יוחנן's view. This step says no. רבי יוחנן has a special פסוק about interest, so his ruling tells us nothing about the general rule. The next step brings that פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Logical reasoning
Verses (plural of קְרָא)
They argue / disagree

phrases.english: He said to him:
There, do they argue about logic?
phrases.notes: 'There' means the argument about returning interest that we just read.

phrases.english: There, they argue about verses!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם בִּסְבָרָא פְּלִיגִי? הָתָם בִּקְרָאֵי פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the attempt to use step 1 as a source for the general question of whether a forbidden act takes effect.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects tying the interest argument to the general logic of whether a forbidden act takes effect.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוחנן's ruling comes from a specific פסוק about interest, not from general logic.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps the big question of אביי and רבא open. Their argument cannot be settled from the laws of interest.

steps.title: רבי יצחק's verse: 'He shall not live'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק learns רבי יוחנן's view from יחזקאל: the lender is punished with his life, but the money is not returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יצחק said: What is the reason of רבי יוחנן? The verse says: 'He gave on interest and took increase, shall he then live? He shall not live.' He is given over to lose his life, and not to returning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the last step's claim by showing the actual פסוק behind רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes the lender's punishment as a matter of 'life'. It does not mention any repayment. רבי יצחק reads this to mean that the consequence of taking interest is a punishment from Heaven, not giving the money back through בית דין. So רבי יוחנן's ruling is a special rule for interest.

keyTerms.meaning: Interest; literally 'a bite'
Increase; another word for interest
For returning (giving back the money)
It is given over to life: the punishment touches his life

phrases.english: As רבי יצחק said:
What is the reason of רבי יוחנן?
The verse says:
'He gave on interest and took increase,'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 18:13

phrases.english: 'shall he then live? He shall not live,'
It is given over to life, and not to returning.
phrases.notes: He means: the lender pays with his life in Heaven's judgment, but the money isn't given back.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up step 2 by showing that רבי יוחנן's view comes from a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן's ruling is based on a פסוק, not on general logic.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 18:13: 'shall he then live? He shall not live.'

steps.title: רב אחא בר אדא's verse: 'Fear your God'
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר אדא learns the same idea from 'and you shall fear your God'. The matter is left to fear of Heaven, not to returning the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר אדא said, from here: 'And you shall fear your God... I am ה׳.' I gave it over to fear, and not to returning.
steps.whatsHappening: A second sage gives a different פסוק as the source for רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים about interest in ויקרא end with 'fear your God'. They do not order the lender to pay back. This suggests that the issue is left between the lender and ה׳. The conclusion is the same as רבי יצחק's: the interest is not returned through בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: Fear (of Heaven)
'And you shall fear your God'
From here (introducing a different source)

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא אָמַר מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: רב אחא בר אדא said, from here:
'And you shall fear your God... I am ה׳' —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:36–38, the פסוקים forbidding interest.

phrases.english: I gave it over to fear, and not to returning.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק for the same ruling of רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: That interest is not returned through בית דין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 25:36: 'and you shall fear your God.'

steps.title: רבא's source: lenders compared to murderers
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns it from a הקש in יחזקאל. Lenders on interest are compared to murderers, and just as murder cannot be undone, interest-lending is not 'undone' by giving the money back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, from here: 'He did all these abominations, he shall surely die, his blood shall be upon him,' and 'He fathered a son who is a robber, a shedder of blood.' Lenders on interest are compared to murderers. Just as murderers are not given to returning, so too lenders on interest are not given to returning.
steps.whatsHappening: A third source for רבי יוחנן's view: רבא compares lenders on interest to murderers using פסוקים from the same chapter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same chapter of יחזקאל speaks about the murderer and about the lender on interest. It gives the lender the same death language: 'his blood shall be upon him.' This links the two sins (a הקש). A murderer cannot fix his sin by 'giving back', and in the same way the lender's sin is not handled by returning the money through בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: They were compared (by a הֶקֵּשׁ, a link drawn from the פסוקים)
People who lend with interest
Shedders of blood: murderers
Abominations

steps.whatToRemember: All three sources (רבי יצחק, רב אחא בר אדא, רבא) back up רבי יוחנן: interest is punished by Heaven, but בית דין does not force it back. Because this comes from פסוקים, it cannot prove the general rule about whether forbidden acts take effect.

phrases.english: רבא said, from here:
'He did all these abominations, he shall surely die,'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 18:13, the same פסוק about the lender on interest.

phrases.english: 'his blood shall be upon him,'
'and he fathered a son who is a robber, a shedder of blood' —
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 18:10

phrases.english: Lenders on interest are compared to murderers:

phrases.aramaic: מָה שׁוֹפְכֵי דָּמִים לֹא נִיתְּנוּ לְהִישָּׁבוֹן,
phrases.english: just as murderers are not given to returning,
phrases.notes: A murder can't be 'given back'.

phrases.aramaic: אַף מַלְוֵי רִבִּית לֹא נִיתְּנוּ לְהִישָּׁבוֹן.
phrases.english: so too lenders on interest are not given to returning.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, different פסוק-based source for the same ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That interest is not returned through בית דין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A הקש between lenders on interest and murderers, from יחזקאל 18:10 and 18:13.
steps.whyThisMatters: It confirms that רבי יוחנן's view rests on פסוקים, so it cannot be used as proof in the argument between אביי and רבא.

steps.title: The verse behind רבי אלעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that רבי אלעזר, who holds that רבית קצוצה is taken back, learns it from 'that your brother may live with you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן בר יצחק said: What is רבי אלעזר's reason? The פסוק says, 'that your brother may live with you.' Give the money back to him, so that he can live with you.
steps.whatsHappening: Steps 3–5 brought sources for רבי יוחנן's view that interest is not returned. Now the גמרא brings the source for the other side, רבי אלעזר, who holds that it is returned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reads 'and your brother shall live with you' as a command: give the borrower back his money so he can keep living alongside you. This backs up step 2, where we said the argument is about how to read פסוקים, not about logic.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That your brother may live with you' (ויקרא 25:36)
Give it back to him
Reason, source

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Elazar?
For the verse says: "that your brother may live with you"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:36

phrases.english: Give it back to him,
so that he can live with you.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the opposite view, after the sources for רבי יוחנן in steps 3–5.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's ruling that רבית קצוצה is taken back by בית דין

steps.title: So what do אביי and רבא argue about?
steps.stepSummary: If the interest argument is only about reading פסוקים, then what is the real argument between אביי and רבא?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what do אביי and רבא argue about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. If the interest question is not the root of the argument between אביי and רבא, where do they actually disagree? This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 cut the link between the interest question and the argument of אביי and רבא. That leaves us without any case where their argument makes a real difference. The גמרא wants to find one.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they argue?

phrases.english: But then, about what
do Abaye and Rava disagree?
phrases.notes: They argue whether something the Torah forbids still takes effect if a person goes ahead and does it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the rejection in step 2: now that interest is not the root of the argument, what is?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical or theoretical point of disagreement between אביי and רבא

steps.title: They argue only about the general rule
steps.stepSummary: The answer: they argue about whether an act done against the Torah takes effect, as a general starting point.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue about whether a deviation takes effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אביי and רבא may not disagree about any specific case. They argue only about the general principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's default is that a forbidden act still works unless a פסוק says otherwise. רבא's default is that it does not work. So they agree on the cases, but they argue about which cases are the rule and which are the exceptions.

keyTerms.meaning: A change, here meaning acting differently from what the Torah commands
Takes effect, works

phrases.english: About whether a deviation takes effect.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשִׁינּוּי קוֹנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Their argument is about the general principle (whether a deviation takes effect), not about one practical case.

steps.title: Another version: they argue about returning fixed interest
steps.stepSummary: A second version says אביי and רבא do argue about רבית קצוצה: אביי says it is not returned, and רבא says it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: according to the answers we gave, they argue about רבית קצוצה. According to אביי, the lender does not return the interest. According to רבא, he does return it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the question of step 7. In this version, the argument of אביי and רבא does show up in a real case: returning fixed interest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, a forbidden act takes effect, so the lender owns the interest and keeps it. For רבא, it does not take effect, so the interest still belongs to the borrower and must be returned. This version keeps the link that step 2 had cut.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the discussion
Fixed interest, set openly at the time of the loan (forbidden by the Torah)
Gives back, returns

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 8. In step 8 there is no practical difference between them; in this version there is one: whether the interest is returned.

phrases.english: Another version:
According to the answers that we answered,
they argue about fixed interest:
according to Abaye, he does not return the interest;
according to Rava, he returns the interest.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative answer to step 7's question, instead of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue about returning רבית קצוצה: אביי says it is not returned, רבא says it is.

steps.title: But אביי also holds fixed interest is taken back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second version: אביי himself holds that judges take back רבית קצוצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But אביי also holds that the judges take back רבית קצוצה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the version in step 9, which said that according to אביי the interest is not returned. It claims that אביי holds the opposite, and the proof comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אביי also says the interest is taken back, then אביי and רבא agree on this case. In that case the interest question cannot be the place where they disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: We take out, we take back (by force of the court)
Judges, the court

phrases.english: But Abaye too holds
that we take back fixed interest through the judges!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אַבָּיֵי נָמֵי סָבַר מַפְּקִינַן רִיבִּית קְצוּצָה בְּדַיָּינִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the alternative version in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 9 that according to אביי the interest is not returned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי's own ruling elsewhere shows that he holds בית דין does take back רבית קצוצה.

steps.title: The case of the cloak worth five for four
steps.stepSummary: The proof: in the case of the cloak, אביי says the court takes back four, and רבא says five. Either way, both take back רבית קצוצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For אביי said: Someone is owed four זוז of interest by his friend. The borrower gave the lender a cloak worth five in place of the four. When we take it back from the lender, we take back four, and the extra זוז was a gift. רבא said: We take back five. Why? All of it came to him as interest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the challenge of step 10 from a ruling of אביי. אביי and רבא argue only about the extra זוז, but both agree that the court takes back the interest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי says 'we take back four.' That means he holds the court forces the lender to return רבית קצוצה, which goes against step 9. רבא takes back all five, because the whole cloak was given as interest. The challenge stands, and step 12 drops the second version because of it.

keyTerms.meaning: Has a money claim against his fellow
A cloak
A gift
Given as interest, under the label of interest

steps.whatToRemember: Even אביי says that בית דין takes back רבית קצוצה (at least the four זוז). So the version that has אביי say 'not returned' runs into trouble.

phrases.english: For Abaye said:
This one who has a claim against his fellow
of four zuz in interest,
and the borrower gave the lender
(in his store) [in place of them]
phrases.notes: Some versions have 'in his store' (round brackets); the corrected wording is 'in place of them' (square brackets), meaning in place of the four זוז.

phrases.english: a cloak worth five, for four,
when we take it back from him,
we take back four from him,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי זוּזָא בְּמַתָּנָה הוּא דִּיהַב לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: and this extra zuz, he gave it to him as a gift.
And Rava said:
We take back five from him.
What is the reason?
All of it, as interest,
came into his hands!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָדֵין דְּמַסֵּיק בְּחַבְרֵיהּ אַרְבַּע זוּזֵי בְּרִיבִּיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the proof for the challenge of step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That אביי holds the court takes back רבית קצוצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: אביי's ruling in the case of the cloak worth five given for four זוז of interest

steps.title: Back to the first answer: they argue about whether a change takes effect
steps.stepSummary: Since the second version fell, the גמרא returns to the first answer: אביי and רבא argue about whether an act that goes against the Torah takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when אביי and רבא argue, it is about whether a change against the Torah takes effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The second version from step 9 was just disproved, so the גמרא goes back to the first answer. אביי and רבא argue only about the general question of whether an act done against the Torah takes effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 showed that both אביי and רבא make the lender give back רבית קצוצה. So they cannot be arguing about that. Their argument must be about the general rule, as step 8 said.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'a change acquires.' Here it means: does an act that changes what the Torah says still take effect?
They argue / disagree

steps.whatToRemember: The argument between אביי and רבא is about a general starting point. It is not about the specific case of רבית קצוצה, because both agree that it is taken back.

phrases.english: Rather, when they disagree,
Abaye and Rava, it is about whether a change takes effect.
phrases.notes: 'שינוי קונה' here means: does something done against the Torah still work? This is the same idea from step 8.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כִּי קָא מִיפַּלְגִי אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since steps 10 and 11 disproved the second version, the גמרא goes back to the first answer from step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביי and רבא argue only about the general question of whether an act done against the Torah takes effect.

steps.title: 'Do not offer' a blemished animal means 'do not consecrate' it
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks why the פסוק says 'you shall not offer' a blemished animal. It answers that the פסוק means 'do not consecrate' it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'Whatever has a blemish, you shall not offer.' Why does the פסוק say this? If it means 'do not slaughter,' that is already written further down. Rather, 'do not offer' means 'do not consecrate.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. A ברייתא explains that 'do not offer' a בעל מום means you may not even make it הקדש for the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not repeat itself for no reason. Since 'do not slaughter' is taught by a later פסוק, this earlier פסוק must be teaching something else. It is teaching that you may not consecrate a blemished animal.

keyTerms.meaning: A blemish or physical defect that makes an animal unfit for a קרבן
Why does the פסוק need to say this? (asks what new thing a פסוק teaches)
Do not consecrate (do not make it הקדש)
Below, meaning later in the same passage

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"Whatever has a blemish, you shall not offer"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:20

phrases.english: Why does the verse need to say this?
If it is teaching "do not slaughter"
that is already stated below!
phrases.notes: The גמרא will show where this is written in steps 15 and 16.

phrases.english: Rather, why does the verse say "do not offer"?
It means "do not consecrate."

steps.title: The list of prohibitions for a blemished animal brought to the altar
steps.stepSummary: From this the Sages say that someone who consecrates blemished animals for the מזבח breaks five prohibitions. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה adds collecting the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: one who consecrates blemished animals for the מזבח breaks five prohibitions: 'do not offer' (meaning 'do not consecrate'), 'do not slaughter,' 'do not sprinkle the blood,' 'do not burn all of it,' and 'do not burn part of it.' steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא uses the reading from step 13 to list each separate prohibition a person can break with a blemished animal set aside for the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each stage of bringing the קרבן has its own prohibition: consecrating, slaughtering, sprinkling the blood, and burning it all or part of it. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה adds one more stage: collecting the blood.

steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going through the פסוק about blemished animals and learns a new prohibition: you may not put a blemished animal on the fires of the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the extra word, you might think the prohibition only applies when the whole animal is burned. The word 'מהם' (of them) shows that burning even some of its parts is forbidden too.

steps.title: Sprinkling the blood, and including the scapegoat
steps.stepSummary: 'על המזבח' forbids sprinkling the blood of a blemished animal. 'לה׳' adds the שעיר המשתלח to the prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do I know sprinkling the blood is forbidden? The פסוק says 'upon the altar.' 'To the Lord' comes to include the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the פסוק. It learns that sprinkling a blemished animal's blood is forbidden, and that the word 'לה׳' adds the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood is not burned, so 'fires' alone would not cover it. 'על המזבח' covers anything put on the מזבח, including the blood. The שעיר המשתלח is not offered on the מזבח at all, yet 'לה׳' includes it, so it too may not be blemished.

steps.title: Does 'to the Lord' really include? A different ברייתא about slaughtering outside

steps.title: The other ברייתא uses 'to ה׳' to exclude the scapegoat
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא about שחוטי חוץ finishes. It says 'לה׳' leaves out the פרה אדומה and the שעיר המשתלח, because they are not set aside only for ה׳ as offerings. This is the opposite of how our ברייתא used 'לה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: I might leave out the בדק הבית animals, but not the פרה אדומה and the שעיר המשתלח, since they are fit to be brought to the entrance of the אהל מועד. So the פסוק says 'לה׳': only animals set aside just for ה׳ count. These two are left out, since they are not set aside just for ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא it started in step 19. The ending shows that this ברייתא uses 'לה׳' to leave out the שעיר המשתלח, which is the opposite of our ברייתא in step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אל פתח אהל מועד' only removed animals that are unfit for the entrance, like בדק הבית animals. The פרה אדומה and the שעיר המשתלח are unblemished, so they could have been included. Then 'לה׳' removes them, since they are not offerings given only to ה׳. So here 'לה׳' leaves something out, while in step 18 'לה׳' added the שעיר המשתלח.

steps.title: It depends on the words around 'to ה׳' in each verse
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that in the שחוטי חוץ פסוק, 'ואל פתח' is broad, so 'לה׳' narrows it. In our פסוק, 'אשה' is narrow, so 'לה׳' widens it.

In our פסוק, 'אשה' (a fire offering) limits the rule to animals burned on the מזבח, which would leave out the שעיר המשתלח. So 'לה׳' must be there to add it back.

steps.title: Why is a verse needed if the lottery only works on fit animals?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא implies that without 'לה׳' a blemished שעיר המשתלח would be allowed. But the יום כיפור lottery only works on an animal fit for both roles, so a blemished goat could never become the שעיר המשתלח anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא implies that only because the פסוק wrote 'לה׳' may one not bring a blemished שעיר המשתלח. Without 'לה׳', I would have said a blemished שעיר המשתלח is fine. But the lottery only sets an animal's role if the animal is fit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for the word 'לה׳' in our ברייתא. It argues the rule would be true even without the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור, two goats go into a lottery; one becomes an offering to ה׳ and one becomes the שעיר המשתלח. Each goat must be fit to be either one. A blemished goat cannot be an offering, so it cannot enter the lottery, and so it can never become the שעיר המשתלח. That makes 'לה׳' seem unneeded.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows חנן המצרי, who allows pairing without a lottery
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the ברייתא follows חנן המצרי. He holds that if the שעיר המשתלח is lost even after the other goat's blood is in the cup, a new goat is brought and paired without a lottery. For that goat, 'לה׳' is needed to forbid a blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Whose view is this? It is חנן המצרי, who said: even if the blood is already in the cup, he brings another goat and pairs it with the first one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the challenge by naming whose view the ברייתא follows. In that view, a שעיר המשתלח can sometimes be chosen without a lottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lottery argument only works when a lottery is held. According to חנן המצרי, a replacement goat can be paired straight away with the already-slaughtered goat, with no lottery. So without 'לה׳' we might think that replacement could be blemished, and the פסוק is needed after all.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every שעיר המשתלח goes through the lottery, so it must already be fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to חנן המצרי, a replacement goat is paired without a lottery, so 'לה׳' is needed to forbid a blemished one.

steps.title: חנן המצרי never said the new goat skips the lottery
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף's first answer. חנן המצרי only taught that the remaining goat is not pushed aside. He never taught that the new goat is chosen without a lottery.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, you learned from חנן המצרי that there is no pushing aside. But did you learn from him that no lottery is needed? Maybe the כהן brings new goats and holds a lottery!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יוסף's answer from step 24. It says חנן המצרי's view does not prove that a new goat could become the שעיר המשתלח without a lottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף needed a case where a goat becomes the שעיר המשתלח without a lottery. Only then could a blemished goat slip in, and only then would 'לה׳' be needed. חנן המצרי only taught that the slaughtered goat's partner is not rejected (no דיחוי). Maybe he still requires a new pair and a fresh lottery, and a lottery only works on unblemished animals. So the question of why 'לה׳' is needed comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, fine (we accept this part)
Being pushed aside, rejected from use
The יום כיפור lottery that decides which goat is for ה׳ and which goes to עזאזל
Perhaps, maybe

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two ideas. 'No דיחוי' means the leftover goat is still usable. 'No lottery' means the new goat gets its role without a lottery. חנן המצרי only clearly said the first.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חנן המצרי's view only proves there is no דיחוי. It does not prove the new goat skips the lottery, so a blemished goat still could not become the שעיר המשתלח.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, who says no lottery
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף changes his answer. The ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, who clearly rules that if one goat dies, its replacement is brought without a lottery.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: Whose view is this ברייתא? It is רבי שמעון's. As a ברייתא teaches: If one of the goats died, the כהן brings a partner for the other without a lottery. These are the words of רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a new answer. He says the ברייתא matches רבי שמעון, who openly says the replacement goat needs no lottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון says this outright: when one goat dies, the new one is brought 'בלא הגרלה', without a lottery. So a goat can become the שעיר המשתלח without passing through a lottery. Without 'לה׳' we might think that goat could be blemished. That is why 'לה׳' is needed to forbid it.

steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, who clearly rules a replacement goat is brought with no lottery, so 'לה׳' is needed to forbid a blemish
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא can save a ברייתא by finding a תנא whose ruling creates the exact case the ברייתא needs.

steps.title: A goat blemished on יום כיפור with its holiness moved to another
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer. 'לה׳' is needed when the שעיר המשתלח became blemished on יום כיפור itself and the כהן transferred its holiness onto another goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The word is only needed for a case where the goat became blemished on that same day, and the כהן transferred its holiness onto another goat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers another way to explain why 'לה׳' is needed. He does not rely on a special תנא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's case, the second goat does not get its role through a lottery. It gets it because the holiness of the blemished goat was transferred onto it. Since no lottery is involved, we might have thought that goat could be blemished. 'לה׳' teaches that it cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (this specific case)
Became blemished

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers explain why 'לה׳' forbids a blemished שעיר המשתלח, even though the lottery only works on fit animals. רב יוסף says it follows רבי שמעון: a replacement goat is brought with no lottery. רבא says it is about a goat blemished on יום כיפור whose holiness was transferred to another goat.
